properties.name: Central District
properties.description: Northern Adelaide metropolitan corridor (Elizabeth, Salisbury, Gawler) plus the Barossa Valley and Light regional recruitment zone.
properties.famous_players: John Platten, Ian Callinan, Sonny Morey
properties.trivia: Central District entered the league in 1964 and created a football heartland in Adelaide's northern industrial suburbs, culminating in 9 flags in 11 years (2000–2010).

properties.name: Glenelg
properties.description: South-western coastal metropolitan strip (Brighton, Glenelg, Marion) plus the fertile Limestone Coast & South East (Mount Gambier, Naracoorte, Millicent).
properties.famous_players: Stephen Kernahan, Tony McGuinness, John Nicholls, Chris McDermott
properties.trivia: The Tigers' country zone in the South East has historically produced some of Australian football's greatest champions, including Carlton captain Stephen Kernahan.

properties.name: North Adelaide
properties.description: Inner-northern suburbs (Prospect, Walkerville, Enfield) extending to the Upper Spencer Gulf, Port Pirie, Flinders Ranges, and the Far North (Roxby Downs).
properties.famous_players: Barrie Robran, Ken Farmer, Darren Jarman, Andrew Jarman
properties.trivia: North Adelaide's sprawling regional country zone reaches deep into the outback. Ken Farmer kicked 1,417 career goals for the Roosters at Prospect.

properties.name: Norwood
properties.description: Adelaide eastern suburbs (The Parade, Kensington, Burnside, Campbelltown) plus the vast, rugged Eyre Peninsula (Port Lincoln, Ceduna, Kimba).
properties.famous_players: Michael Aish, Garry McIntosh, Michael Taylor, Craig Balme
properties.trivia: Norwood's Eyre Peninsula pipeline is legendary, producing hardened country footballers that powered the Redlegs to 31 SANFL premierships.

properties.name: Port Adelaide
properties.description: Historic docklands, LeFevre Peninsula, Semaphore, Alberton, and Far West Coast regional recruitment.
properties.famous_players: Russell Ebert, Fos Williams, Bob Quinn, Greg Phillips, Tim Ginever
properties.trivia: The most successful club in Australian football history with 36 SANFL premierships. Fos Williams established their famous club creed at Alberton in 1962.

properties.name: South Adelaide
properties.description: Outer southern metropolitan corridor (Noarlunga, Christies Beach, Morphett Vale, Aldinga), Fleurieu Peninsula, and Kangaroo Island.
properties.famous_players: Rick Davies, Mark Bickley, Craig McRae, Peter Darley
properties.trivia: Foundation SANFL club. Both 1997/98 Crows premiership captain Mark Bickley and Collingwood premiership coach Craig McRae hail from South Adelaide's southern zone.

properties.name: Sturt
properties.description: Affluent inner-south (Unley, Mitcham, Belair, Blackwood) expanding through the Adelaide Hills and Murraylands (Mount Barker, Murray Bridge).
properties.famous_players: Paul Bagshaw, Jack Oatey, Rick Davies, John Halbert, Tony Burgan
properties.trivia: Master coach Jack Oatey revolutionized modern Australian football at Unley Oval with precision handball and checkside kicking in the 1960s and 1970s.

properties.name: West Adelaide
properties.description: Western inner-suburbs (Richmond, Mile End, Hilton, Keswick) and the sprawling Riverland & Mallee (Renmark, Berri, Loxton, Waikerie).
properties.famous_players: Neil Kerley, Mark Mickan, Brian Leys, Bruce Lindner
properties.trivia: Neil Kerley famously captained-coached the Bloods to the 1961 flag and coached them to the unforgettable 1983 premiership against Sturt at Football Park.

properties.name: Woodville-West Torrens
properties.description: Unified western coastal territory (Woodville, West Lakes, Grange, Henley Beach) plus the entire Yorke Peninsula.
properties.famous_players: Malcolm Blight, Bob Hank, Lindsay Head, Andrew McLeod, Matthew Pavlich
properties.trivia: Formed in 1991 by the merger of the Woodville Warriors and West Torrens Eagles. The merged club has claimed five SANFL premierships since inception.
